question: A short course of oral prednisolone can safely bridge a patient with chronic plaque psoriasis to maintenance therapy because the rapid clearance prevents prolonged steroid exposure.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is false and represents a dangerous misconception. Systemic corticosteroids are contraindicated in psoriasis — their withdrawal can trigger a rebound generalised pustular or erythrodermic flare, which is a dermatological emergency, even after a short course.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is false. Systemic corticosteroids are contraindicated in psoriasis regardless of the course length. Although they may transiently clear the skin, their withdrawal can precipitate a life-threatening rebound into generalised pustular (Von Zumbusch) or erythrodermic psoriasis.
